404.1 Lane sign. This sign requires the driver to drive in the lane or part of the carriageway that the sign refers to.
404.2 Lane sign. This sign requires the driver to drive in the lane or part of the carriageway that the sign refers to.
405 Lane sign. This sign requires the driver to drive on either side of the sign where the road splits in two but comes together again further on.
406 Roundabout. This sign indicates that you are driving into a roundabout. The arrows indicate the direction of travel in the roundabout.
410 Cycle path. This sign indicates that a path is intended solely for bicycles and light mopeds of class I.
412 Footpath. This sign indicates that a path is intended mainly for pedestrians.
414 Bridle path. This sign indicates that a path is intended specifically for horse riders.

416.1 Shared path. This sign indicates that a path is intended solely for the traffic shown on the sign. The sign is varied according to the type of traffic. Road users shall show each other mutual consideration.

416.2 Shared path. This sign indicates that a path is intended solely for the traffic shown on the sign. The sign is varied according to the type of traffic. Road users shall show each other mutual consideration.

418.1 Segregated paths. This sign indicates two parallel paths that are separated by a surface marking, a difference in level, an island or something comparable. The sign is varied according to the type of traffic. The position of the symbols on the sign indicates which path is intended for which type of traffic.
